notes: Used by collectors\storage\windows\G1-storage.ps1. Edit freely; no code change needed.
'*' = part of one folder name, '**' = any number of folders. The last segment must be literal, or else the parent must be literal.
First matching rule wins per folder; across folders the outermost match wins (nothing is counted twice).

Optional: exclude / excludeSet, requireChild (any exists inside), requireSibling (any exists next to it), idleDays (parent project untouched N days), minBytes, special (temp-age | nvm-inactive | node-shadowed). how may use {version}.

dirRules.purpose: Windows component store (system files and updates). Much of it is hard links to files elsewhere in Windows, so the size shown overstates real use.
dirRules.how: Never delete by hand. To trim superseded components run, as admin: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup

dirRules.purpose: Cached .msi/.msp files Windows needs to repair, update or uninstall programs.
dirRules.how: Never delete by hand (breaks uninstall/repair). Uninstall programs you no longer need instead.

dirRules.purpose: Setup bundles kept so the programs can be repaired or uninstalled.
dirRules.how: Leave it. Uninstall the related programs in Settings > Apps instead.

dirRules.purpose: Previous Windows installation kept after an upgrade (allows rollback for about 10 days).
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > tick 'Previous Windows installation(s)' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Downloaded Windows Update packages; installed ones are no longer needed.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Windows Update Cleanup' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Delivery Optimization cache: update pieces shared with other PCs.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Delivery Optimization Files' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Windows and installer temporary files.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Temporary files' > Remove files (this folder needs admin).

dirRules.purpose: Your temporary files. Only files older than 7 days are counted.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Temporary files' > Remove files (or turn on Storage Sense). Files in use are skipped automatically.

dirRules.purpose: Leftover app-updater downloads.
dirRules.how: Recycle the folder's contents when no app update is running.

dirRules.purpose: Memory dumps written when programs crashed; only useful for debugging those crashes.
dirRules.how: If you are not troubleshooting a crash with a vendor, recycle the .dmp files.

dirRules.purpose: Queued and archived crash/error reports.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Windows error reports and feedback diagnostics' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Blue-screen and kernel diagnostic dumps.
dirRules.how: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > 'System error memory dump files' (admin).

dirRules.purpose: Deleted files still waiting in the Recycle Bin.
dirRules.how: Open the Recycle Bin, restore anything you still need, then 'Empty Recycle Bin'.

dirRules.purpose: Web browser cache (copies of web pages, images, scripts). Rebuilt automatically.
dirRules.how: Clear in browser: Settings > Privacy > Clear browsing data > tick only 'Cached images and files' (keeps passwords, cookies and history).

dirRules.purpose: Legacy Internet Explorer / Office web cache.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'Temporary Internet Files' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Compiled graphics shaders; rebuilt when games/apps run.
dirRules.how: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > 'DirectX Shader Cache' > Remove files.

dirRules.purpose: Editor caches: compiled code of past editor versions, downloaded extension packages, old logs. Rebuilt as needed.
dirRules.how: Close every VS Code / Cursor window, then recycle this folder; the editor recreates what it needs.

dirRules.purpose: npm download cache (a copy of every package version ever installed).
dirRules.how: Run: npm cache clean --force (projects re-download what they need).

dirRules.purpose: pip download/wheel cache.
dirRules.how: Run: pip cache purge

dirRules.purpose: pnpm package store. Projects hard-link from it, so real savings can be smaller than shown.
dirRules.how: Run: pnpm store prune (removes packages no project uses).

dirRules.purpose: Yarn package cache.
dirRules.how: Run: yarn cache clean

dirRules.purpose: NuGet package cache.
dirRules.how: Run: dotnet nuget locals all --clear

dirRules.purpose: Gradle dependency and wrapper cache.
dirRules.how: Run gradle --stop (or close Android Studio), then recycle the folder; it is re-downloaded on the next build.

dirRules.purpose: Downloaded Rust crates and sources.
dirRules.how: Close editors/builds, then recycle registry\cache and registry\src; Cargo re-downloads on the next build.

dirRules.purpose: Maven dependency cache.
dirRules.how: Recycle it when no build is running; Maven re-downloads on the next build.

dirRules.purpose: uv package cache.
dirRules.how: Run: uv cache clean

dirRules.purpose: Go build and module cache.
dirRules.how: Run: go clean -cache -modcache

dirRules.purpose: Conda package downloads.
dirRules.how: Run: conda clean --all

dirRules.purpose: Bun package cache.
dirRules.how: Run: bun pm cache rm

dirRules.purpose: Downloaded Electron/Node headers/test-browser binaries; re-downloaded on demand.
dirRules.how: Recycle when no build or test is running.

dirRules.purpose: Test browsers downloaded by Playwright.
dirRules.how: Run in a project that uses Playwright: npx playwright uninstall --all (they re-install with npx playwright install).

dirRules.purpose: AI models and datasets downloaded from Hugging Face.
dirRules.how: Run: huggingface-cli delete-cache and untick the models you still use; others re-download on demand.

dirRules.purpose: Local AI models downloaded by Ollama.
dirRules.how: Run: ollama list, then ollama rm <model> for models you no longer use.

dirRules.purpose: Local AI models downloaded by LM Studio.
dirRules.how: LM Studio > My Models > delete models you no longer use.

dirRules.purpose: Docker Desktop's WSL disk images: all images, containers, volumes and build cache.
dirRules.how: In Docker Desktop delete unused images, containers and volumes (or docker system prune -a after checking). The .vhdx only shrinks after Docker Desktop compacts it; never delete the file by hand.

dirRules.purpose: Android emulator devices and system images.
dirRules.how: Android Studio > Device Manager (delete unused devices) and SDK Manager (untick unused system images).

dirRules.purpose: Node.js version installed by nvm but not the active one.
dirRules.how: Check no project needs it (.nvmrc / engines.node), then run: nvm uninstall {version}

dirRules.purpose: Separate Node.js {version} install that is shadowed: 'node' on PATH resolves to another copy (nvm), so this one is unused.
dirRules.how: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Node.js > Uninstall. nvm keeps providing node; check with 'node -v' afterwards.

dirRules.purpose: McAfee (WebAdvisor) files, often left behind after a bundled trial was removed.
dirRules.how: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > McAfee WebAdvisor > Uninstall. If it is not listed, these are leftovers: use McAfee's official removal tool (MCPR).

dirRules.purpose: Driver installers, logs or recovery files left by the PC maker (eSupport = ASUS/MyASUS) or driver setups.
dirRules.how: Keep if you may need to reinstall drivers or use the maker's recovery; otherwise copy to an external drive, then remove.

dirRules.purpose: Git worktrees created by coding agents (extra working copies of a repo).
dirRules.how: Check storage G2 projectCopies for uncommitted/unpushed work and push it; then remove each one with 'git worktree remove <path>' from the main repo.

dirRules.purpose: Extra copy of a project folder (merge/isolation copy or Explorer copy).
dirRules.how: Check storage G2 projectCopies (uncommitted / unpushed / stashes) first; when nothing is at risk, move it to a holding folder or recycle it.

dirRules.purpose: Backup folder.
dirRules.how: Confirm the data also exists elsewhere (the original project, an external drive or cloud) before removing.

dirRules.purpose: Python virtual environment (installed packages), recreatable from the project's requirements.
dirRules.how: Find the project that uses it (requirements.txt / pyproject.toml), recycle it, and recreate later with python -m venv + pip install -r requirements.txt.

dirRules.purpose: Installed npm packages of a project untouched for 90+ days.
dirRules.how: Check the project still has package.json and a lockfile, then recycle node_modules; 'npm install' restores it.

dirRules.purpose: Python virtual environment of a project untouched for 90+ days.
dirRules.how: Check requirements.txt / pyproject.toml exists, then recycle it; recreate with python -m venv + pip install -r requirements.txt.

dirRules.purpose: Build cache/output of a project untouched for 90+ days; regenerated on the next build.
dirRules.how: Recycle it; the next build or dev run regenerates it.

dirRules.purpose: Build output of a project untouched for 90+ days; regenerated by building again.
dirRules.how: Make sure nothing in it is the only copy of a release you need, then recycle it.

dirRules.purpose: Cache of a desktop app (Discord, Slack, Teams, Electron apps...). Rebuilt automatically.
dirRules.how: Quit the app completely (also from the tray), then recycle the folder; the app rebuilds it.

fileRules.how: Managed by Windows. Size only via System > Advanced system settings > Performance > Virtual memory (not recommended).
Do not delete. To shrink, as admin: powercfg /h /type reduced; to remove: powercfg /h off (disables hibernation and Fast Startup).

fileRules.purpose: Full memory dump from a blue-screen crash.
fileRules.how: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > 'System error memory dump files' (admin).
Run 'wsl -l -v'. Remove distros you no longer use with 'wsl --unregister <name>' (erases everything inside). For kept ones free space inside Linux, then: wsl --manage <name> --set-sparse true.

fileRules.purpose: Installer or archive downloaded more than 30 days ago.
fileRules.how: Recycle it if the program is installed or the archive was extracted; most can be downloaded again.

fileRules.purpose: Leftover temporary copies of Claude Code's settings file (~\.claude.json) from interrupted saves.
fileRules.how: Recycle them; Claude Code never reads these .tmp copies (the real file is ~\.claude.json).

fileRules.purpose: Office owner/lock files (~$name) left behind when Word/Excel/PowerPoint closed abnormally.
fileRules.how: Close Word/Excel/PowerPoint; any ~$ file that is still there is orphaned - recycle it.
If no download is running, recycle it.

extGuessDefault.how: Open it to confirm what it is; keep it, move it to external/cloud storage, or recycle it.

vm-disk.how: Clean up inside the VM, WSL distro or Docker and compact it with its own tool; never delete it while in use.

ai-model.how: Remove it from the app that downloaded it (Ollama, LM Studio, ComfyUI...) if you no longer use it.

database.purpose: Database file used by an app
database.how: Belongs to an app; clean it up from inside that app, never delete the file directly.

mail.how: Archive or clean up mail inside Outlook; never delete the file.

log.how: Recycle it if the app that writes it is closed and you are not troubleshooting it.

crash-dumps.how: Recycle it unless you are troubleshooting that crash.

program-files.how: Remove it by uninstalling the program it belongs to (Settings > Apps).

windows-package.how: Usually managed by Windows or an installer; leave it unless you know where it came from.

git-objects.how: Part of a git repo: run 'git gc' there, or remove the whole repo if unused.
